tool_input.message:
Invariant review of fix/spec-backed-enforcement complete: 2 substantive findings (1 HIGH, 1 MEDIUM), 1 spec-wording gap to report as asked, 1 scope note. Tests in both touched packages pass (go test -race ./internal/mission ./internal/hook: ok, ok).

(1) vaib / PathContainedByFixed — CONFIRMED with one MEDIUM finding.
- splitSegments (conflict.go:530) computes `absolute` from the trimmed, slash-normalized, trailing-slash-trimmed form, exactly CanonicalPathFixed's `raw(1) = rsEmpty` rule; segment computation is unchanged (SegmentationUnchanged holds by inspection of the diff).
- pathContainedBy consults the flag before containment (conflict.go:394). The ethos-vaib case (relative entry, absolute file) is refused and pinned twice: conflict_test.go:568 and pretooluse_test.go:471.
- The widening from the spec's `absolute(file) = zfalse` to flag-equality IS pinned: conflict_test.go "an absolute file IS contained by a matching absolute entry" and the pre-existing pretooluse_test.go "absolute match" row. The absolute allowlist entry is real: verifierAllowlistSplit appends store.ContractPath (subagent_start.go:470-485).
- MEDIUM: the widening's justification is asserted, not demonstrated. pathAllowed is consulted only for Write/Edit targets (extractTargetPath, pretooluse.go:252-266); reads are unrestricted. So the only behavior the strict spec reading would remove is a verifier's ability to Write/Edit its own contract.yaml — nothing in code or tests shows that is needed (results go through the CLI), and the strict reading is arguably safer (a verifier could not edit its own contract mid-review). Also, the spec itself nowhere records the widening; the disclosure lives only in code/test comments, so a future spec re-run will flag the implementation as divergent. Recommend either demonstrating the requirement or adopting the strict reading; at minimum the spec needs a widening note.

(2) loud-skip — HIGH finding. isEvaluatorOfOpenMission (subagent_start.go:700-715) does NOT compute verifierOfOpenMission exactly; it is an under-approximation. missions.List() error returns false; a per-mission Load error is skipped — including when the unloadable mission is the one naming this evaluator. The spec's LoudSkip sets diagnosticEmitted' = ztrue unconditionally ("rather than by a guard that could fail to fire", spec-hook-gates.tex:737-739); the implementation guards on a fallible scan, so SilentDisabledUnreachableUnderLoudSkip does not hold when the store errors. Constructible: open mission naming djb as evaluator, contract unreadable or failing strict decode (version skew is the realistic path), spawn djb with empty MISSION_ID — no diagnostic, no gate, no allowlist: the exact state the spec proves unreachable. The test comment's "whenever the spawn handle is, in fact, the evaluator of an open mission" overstates. Fix: on List/Load error inside the scan, emit a variant diagnostic ("cannot determine whether this handle needed the gate: <err>") instead of returning false silently; add a test pinning it. Otherwise: the guarded-vs-unconditional deviation is a legitimate refinement (quiet ad-hoc spawns), the message satisfies CauseIndistinguishable (names all three causes, guesses none), and both quiet-branch tests are correct.

(3) Update guard — CONFIRMED; the spec paragraph now overstates, exact wording gap as requested. The guard (store.go:914) reads onDisk.Status under flock; the reopen forge is refused and pinned (TestStore_Update_CannotReopenClosedMission). The open->terminal forge remains: with on-disk open, a caller can set Status to closed/failed/escalated/abandoned and Update persists it, bypassing CloseRequiresResult and Abandon's zero-blocking-delegation guard — ethos-w1ii, disclosed in CHANGELOG. Spec statements now false: spec-mission-lifecycle.tex:547-550 ("no c.Status != StatusOpen check anywhere in its body"), 555-558 (the reopen exploit "Update will persist it"), 559-560 ("fix landing separately"), the Non-goals bullet at 120-122 ("carries no status = stOpen guard at all"), and the TerminalIsFinal traceability row at 960-963 (same claim, plus stale line range 873-932). The paragraph should now say: Update carries the same on-disk terminal-state guard as its six siblings (ethos-fhns fixed; guard reads on-disk status, so a caller-side Status forged to open cannot resurrect a terminal mission); the remaining, narrower divergence is that for an on-disk-open mission Update accepts any caller-supplied Status, so open->terminal can be forged past Close's result gate and Abandon's delegation guard (bead ethos-w1ii); TerminalIsFinal therefore holds for Update in the terminal->* direction while *->terminal via Update remains unguarded, and Update stays excluded from the modelled operation set for that reason, not for lacking a guard.

(4) lint — claim holds for H5; residual literal-string coverage checks remain elsewhere in lint.go (MEDIUM). Exactly one containment implementation exists package-wide (pathContainedBy; PathContainedBy wraps it; pretooluse pathAllowed delegates), and lintInputsNotInWriteSet (lint.go:193) has no residual string comparison. But three sibling heuristics still decide directory/glob coverage by literal canonical-string membership — the same ethos-8ady defect class: lintAdjacentTest (lint.go:75, 80), lintReadmeInCriteria (lint.go:131, 134-138), lintInvertedTestGap (lint.go:160, 162). Falsifying case: write_set ["internal/hook/**", "internal/hook/foo.go"] still draws "foo.go has no adjacent foo_test.go in write_set" although the glob authorizes creating the test. The in-diff comment scopes its claim to H5, so the code's own prose is accurate; the lint.go-wide "no residual string comparison" property does not hold. Fix: route the dir-coverage fallbacks in H1/H3/H4 through PathContainedBy as H5 now does.

tool_input.message:
Addendum to the fix round I sent you (combine into the same commit series). The invariant reviewer sharpened the same HIGH: the spec's LoudSkip is UNCONDITIONAL precisely so no fallible guard can fail to fire; your scan is an under-approximation, and the constructible bad case is an open mission naming the spawn handle as evaluator whose contract fails strict decode (version skew) — Load skips it, scan returns false, no diagnostic, no gate: the exact state the spec proves unreachable.

So beyond the per-error stderr warnings from my previous message, add the closing behavior: if the scan encountered ANY List/Load error and found no match, emit a variant diagnostic — "cannot determine whether this spawn needed the verifier gate (mission store error); verifier hash gate and ETHOS_VERIFIER_ALLOWLIST are inactive for this spawn" — so the diagnostic degrades to uncertainty, never to silence. A clean scan with no match stays quiet as before. Also soften the test/doc comment's "whenever the spawn handle is, in fact, the evaluator of an open mission" to reflect the store-error caveat. Add a test: matching mission whose contract is corrupted on disk → skip warning + uncertainty diagnostic emitted, spawn still allowed. Report one commit hash set for the whole round.
